content.text:
Review findings:

- Medium — “Stop” can miss a generation still awaiting SecureStore. `runCompletion` marks busy, then awaits `getProviderKey` before creating/storing an `AbortController` ([KeatingProvider.tsx:214-235](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:214)). `newSession`, session selection, deletion, and clear-data call `stopGeneration`, but it has nothing to abort in that interval ([KeatingProvider.tsx:345-400](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:345)). The credential read can then finish and issue the old request anyway, including after “clear learning data.” Use a generation/operation epoch (checked after credential loading) or allocate a cancellable controller before the await.

- Medium — Forked assistant messages retain source feedback despite receiving new IDs. `createForkedSession` spreads every message, including `feedback`, while replacing only the ID ([session-lineage.ts:32](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/session-lineage.ts:32)). If an original “Helpful” message is forked and the copied response is changed to “Needs work,” global feedback totals are decremented/incremented for the copy ([KeatingProvider.tsx:402-419](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:402)), leaving the original still visibly Helpful while aggregate state says otherwise. Strip feedback during fork, or model feedback as source-message-level identity.

- Low — Cached catalog hydration trusts arbitrary provider and transport strings. `readCachedModelCatalog` only checks those fields are strings ([model-catalog-storage.ts:72-81](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog-storage.ts:72)); selecting such a cached record persists an invalid provider into app state ([KeatingProvider.tsx:477-481](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:477)). On next boot the persisted-state validator rejects it, preserving an unusable record until the user clears data. Validate provider against the five supported IDs, transport against native transports, and finite non-negative bounds before exposing cached rows.

No additional issues found in the live models.dev envelope parsing, native request shaping, normal stream delta handling, or fork tree/action paths.

Verification: `bun test` for the five focused suites passed (35 tests); `bun run typecheck` passed.
I’ll verify the three fixes at their state-transition boundaries and inspect the added tests for the race and validation cases.

content.text:
All three findings are closed.

- Cancellation race: closed. The controller is created and registered before credential I/O, and the post-await `signal.aborted` guard prevents placeholder creation or network streaming after a stop ([KeatingProvider.tsx:214-237](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:214)).

- Fork feedback divergence: closed. Fork clones now remove `feedback`, preserving independent message identity and aggregate feedback accounting ([session-lineage.ts:34-38](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/session-lineage.ts:34)).

- Poisoned cached model records: closed. Cache records now require a supported provider, exact provider transport, canonical key, valid source, and finite non-negative token limits before display ([model-catalog.ts:79-98](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog.ts:79), [model-catalog-storage.ts:23-31](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog-storage.ts:23)).

No regression directly caused by these fixes found. I independently reran the six focused suites: 49 passing; mobile typecheck passes.

One test-quality note only: the fork-feedback assertion currently uses a source fixture with no feedback, so it does not prove stripping. The implementation itself is correct; seed `feedback: "helpful"` in the source assistant fixture to make the regression test meaningful.
